name: Oar Health
one_liner: An online service that prescribes naltrexone to help you drink less or quit, with medication shipped to you and optional coaching.
best_for: Adults who want medication to help them drink less, not only to quit
People who want a quick online start without in-person visits
People paying cash who prefer not to use insurance
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988, or call 911
People who may have dangerous alcohol withdrawal (shaking, seizures, hallucinations) and need medical detox
People who take opioid medicines, which naltrexone blocks
People who want their care billed to insurance
short_description: Online naltrexone prescribing for adults who want to drink less or quit, $99/month billed quarterly; cash-pay, no insurance.
long_description: Oar Health is a US telehealth service for alcohol use. After an online assessment, a licensed clinician can prescribe naltrexone, an FDA-approved medication that reduces cravings and the reward from drinking; it is shipped to you, and you can aim to cut back or quit. Oar also sells a compounded naltrexone mint (Clutch) that is not FDA-approved. Reviews report a one-time $50 assessment fee and $297 every three months (about $99 a month); Oar does not take insurance, though some HSA or FSA plans may pay, and a prescription can be moved to an outside pharmacy that bills insurance. It operates in most US states, only where its clinicians are licensed. Naltrexone itself is well studied for alcohol use disorder, but no published study of Oar's service was found. It is not a detox or withdrawal service.

pricing.notes: Cash-pay; does not bill insurance. Some HSA/FSA plans may pay. A prescription can be transferred to an outside pharmacy that bills insurance. Generic naltrexone is often cheaper through insurance or discount cards.

privacy.notes: Policy (Aug 2025) says it uses targeted or behavioral advertising, shares data with advertising and marketing vendors and takes part in ad networks; whether HIPAA applies was not confirmed.

seo.meta_description: Oar Health provides virtual alcohol treatment with medication and coaching designed for people who want to cut back on drinking, not necessarily quit entirely.

faqs.q: Is Oar Health for people who want to quit drinking?
faqs.a: Oar serves both people who want to quit and those who want to reduce drinking to a healthier level. Their harm reduction approach doesn't require abstinence as a goal. You set your own targets based on what's right for you.

faqs.q: How does Oar Health's medication work?
faqs.a: Oar typically uses naltrexone, which reduces cravings and the reward from alcohol. Some people take it daily; others use it strategically before drinking (the Sinclair Method). Your Oar physician will recommend the best approach for you.

faqs.q: How quickly can I start Oar?
faqs.a: Oar is designed for quick access. Complete an online assessment, have a brief physician consultation, and start medication within days. Coaching begins alongside medication. There's no waitlist or lengthy intake process.
Coverage varies by plan. Some insurance plans cover Oar's services; others don't. They also offer self-pay options. Contact them to check your specific coverage before enrolling.

primary_uses: Naltrexone prescription for drinking less or quitting
Online assessment by a licensed clinician

availability.note: Most US states, only where its clinicians are licensed (reviews report 42 to 49 states). Its Clutch mint is compounded and not FDA-approved.

patient_summary: You complete an online assessment, an Oar clinician reviews it, and if appropriate you are prescribed naltrexone, which is shipped to you. Your goal can be cutting back or stopping. It is cash-pay at about $99 a month (billed $297 every three months) after a $50 assessment; it does not bill insurance.
